payload.headline: 7-day activation fell from 40.1% to 36.9% for cohorts that signed up after Feb 10

cause.does_not_prove: Why Microsoft calendar users stopped activating.
cause.text: The drop is concentrated in Microsoft calendar workspaces: 39.4% before, 29.8% after.

cause.does_not_prove: That the release caused the drop.

evidence.quote: The notetaker joins Zoom calls about 20 seconds sooner.

cause.text: The onset matches rel_0318, Zoom bot: faster join.

payload.cheapest_test: Roll back rel_0318 for Microsoft calendar workspaces and read activation after 7 days.
payload.question: Why did activation fall, and what should we do about it?
payload.recommendation: Roll back the Zoom bot change for Microsoft calendar workspaces.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: That no Teams bot issue exists.

evidence.ref: exploratory: activation by calendar_provider and primary meeting_platform

ruled_out.text: The Teams bot is not the cause. Within Microsoft calendar workspaces, the drop is similar whether meetings run on Zoom or Teams.

size.method: activation gap x conversion gap (activated vs not) x trials per week in the segment x ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Share of blocked orgs whose admin approves within 7 days
would_change_if: Google calendar workspaces also dropped after Feb 10
Microsoft activation was already falling before Feb 10
